title: Finish the JSON Schema subset validator
prompt:
Our schema validator in src/validate.ts only handles type, required and properties so far. Please finish it so validate(schema, data) implements everything in SPEC.md: enum and const with deep equality, the numeric bounds (minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum), minLength/maxLength counted in code points, pattern, additionalProperties (boolean or schema), minItems/maxItems, items, uniqueItems, allOf/anyOf/oneOf, and local $ref including recursive references.

The return shape stays the same: an array of { path, keyword } where path is a JSON Pointer into the data. SPEC.md says where each error is reported, which keywords report their subschemas' errors and which report a single error of their own, when keywords are ignored for other value types, and when SchemaError (src/types.ts) is thrown. Keep the existing behaviour for type, required, properties and boolean schemas, and keep the validate signature unchanged. Splitting the code into more files is fine.
acceptance: Every keyword in SPEC.md: enum/const with deep, order-insensitive object equality and type-strict comparison; inclusive and exclusive bounds; code-point lengths; unanchored unicode patterns; additionalProperties false and as a schema, relative to properties; items with index paths; uniqueItems single error; allOf merging, anyOf/oneOf single errors including oneOf with two matches; $ref to definitions, '#', escaped tokens, recursion, siblings of $ref, SchemaError for unresolvable or non-local refs; JSON Pointer escaping of ~ and /; type-specific keywords ignored on other types; no duplicate errors.
difficulty_rationale: Many keywords with distinct reporting rules that interact (combinators suppress sub-errors, allOf merges them, $ref recursion and escaping, deep equality), so a first pass usually misses several.
